lesson_title: A Drawing You Can Build On. Literally.
hook_text: Tape plastic over your working drawing and build the tower face right on top of it. Every face comes out identical.
clip_script: Before the making lesson, two pieces of paper save the day. First, the resource list: every material with a number and a reason. Four card tube legs, because tubes beat flat strips. Twenty-four straws for horizontals, shorter at each level. Thirty-six for diagonals. String for inside. Base plate, webs, gussets, glue, pins. Then the tools: mat, knife, ruler, pegs for drying joints. Weigh a sheet and a bundle: are you under 150 grams? Fix it on paper now. Second, the working drawing of one face, scale 1 to 2. Centre line, base 150, platform 60, legs leaning in, levels ticked closer at the bottom, X's below, zigzag above, string dashed because it hides behind the face. Every real size, once, in millimetres. Letter the parts, match them to a table. Now the trick: cover the drawing in plastic and glue the straws straight onto it. The drawing becomes the jig. Four identical faces, no guessing.
visual_style: Whiteboard checklist filling with quantities, then a flat dimensioned tower face with lettered parts; a hand lays straws onto the drawing under a plastic sheet.
mood: Practical and reassuring, preparation that pays off.
pacing: Fast list with numbers, steady build of the face drawing, the jig trick as the payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and finish your resource list and one-face drawing before the making lesson.
